<issue identifier="MM-473">
<title>atrium-repo entries_prefixed over-scans: listRecords 500s, and would serve foreign records but for one fallback</title>
<description>
## Verdict: hypothesis (1), prefix over-scan — CONFIRMED

Settled by walking the live exported CAR (6,409 MST entries) with `atrium_repo`'s own `Tree` API. `entries_prefixed(prefix)` yields keys **outside** the requested prefix.

| Collection | Real records | `entries_prefixed` yielded | Leaked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `community.lexicon.calendar.rsvp` | 1 | 2 | `computer.aetheros.id/self` |
| `coop.hypha.spores.social.takenFlower` | 1 | 2 | `dev.cocore.account.profile/self` |
| `dev.cocore.compute.termsAcceptance` | 3 | 4 | `fm.teal.alpha.actor.status/self` |
| `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization` | 5 | **779** | **774 keys** |

The last row rules out "off by one at the boundary": the leak spans `fm.teal.alpha.feed.play/…` through `garden.goals.profile/self` — a contiguous run that **skips** the collections sorting immediately after the prefix (`dev.cocore.compute.provider`, `.receipt`, `.termsAcceptance`). An entire MST subtree is being yielded. The prefix range is not being bounded correctly when it ends at a node boundary.

This is an upstream `atrium-repo` defect (`Tree::entries_prefixed`), but it is ours to defend against.

## There is no data loss

`sync.getRepo` → 200, 3,347,975 bytes. `build_car` reads every reachable CID (commit, MST nodes, and every entry's value CID) and propagates any read failure, so a successful export proves all record blocks are present. The repo is complete.

## Why it currently 500s rather than corrupting

`crates/repo-engine/src/records.rs`, `list_records_json`:

```rust
let strip = |key: &str| key.strip_prefix(&prefix).unwrap_or(key).to_string();
// ...
let full_key = format!("{prefix}{rkey}");
let value = repo.get_raw(&full_key).await?.ok_or(RecordError::NotFound)?;
```

A leaked key lacks `prefix`, so `unwrap_or(key)` keeps it whole and the re-concatenation produces e.g.
`"dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization/garden.goals.profile/self"` — which resolves to nothing → `NotFound` → 500.

**This fallback is the only thing preventing a silent data-integrity breach.** Verified against the real repo: every leaked key resolves successfully under `get_raw` when passed *verbatim*. Had the code reused the original `key` instead of rebuilding one — the natural "optimization" — all 774 foreign records would have been returned to the caller as members of `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization`, with valid CIDs and no error.

Any fix must preserve fail-closed behaviour. Do not "fix" this by passing the original key through.

## Fix

Filter on `strip_prefix`'s `None` instead of `unwrap_or`. Since the stream is ascending and foreign keys sort after the prefix range, `break` on the first non-matching key is both correct and a performance win — today a `limit=100` request against a 5-record collection walks 100 entries.

Secondary: `has_more` / cursor derivation is computed from the polluted `entries` vector and is wrong whenever truncation hides a leak.

## Reproduction without the live repo

`entries.truncate(limit)` runs before the resolve loop, so `limit == count` succeeds and `limit == count + 1` fails. Verified 4/4 live:

```
community.lexicon.calendar.rsvp         limit=1 -> 200   limit=2 -> 500
coop.hypha.spores.social.takenFlower    limit=1 -> 200   limit=2 -> 500
dev.cocore.compute.termsAcceptance      limit=3 -> 200   limit=4 -> 500
dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization limit=5 -> 200   limit=6 -> 500
control: app.bsky.feed.threadgate       limit=100 -> 200
```

## Regression test

Construct a repo whose collection boundary falls on an MST node boundary, then assert `list_records_json` returns exactly that collection's records for every `limit` from 1 to count+5, and never a key from a neighbouring collection. Assert the same for the `reverse` branch, which materialises the whole prefixed stream and is affected identically.

## Follow-ups

* Report upstream to `atrium-repo` with this reproduction.
* Audit other `entries_prefixed` call sites for the same assumption.

## Impact recap

Blocks `blob_gc` reconcile permanently for an affected account (it pages at `RECORD_PAGE_SIZE = 100`, always `> count`), which via <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> destroys every one of that account's blobs 6 hours later. That is what happened on 2026-07-25.
</description>

## Code-level root cause found — chain is now complete

The defect is in `atrium-repo` 0.1.8, `Node::entries_with_prefix` (`src/mst.rs`, \~line 1070):

```rust
if let NodeEntry::Leaf(t) = e {
    // Ensure the specified prefix is not longer than the key.
    // If the key is shorter than the prefix, it is always lexicographically lesser.
    if let Some(kp) = t.key.get(..prefix.len()) {
        match kp.cmp(prefix) { /* Equal → push+continue, Greater → break */ }
    }
}
list.push(e.clone());   // ← intended for Tree entries
```

**A leaf whose key is SHORTER than the prefix makes** `t.key.get(..prefix.len())` **return** `None`**, which skips the comparison entirely and falls through to the unconditional** `push` **meant for subtree pointers.** The comment above states the correct rule; the `if let Some` guard implements its opposite.

This retrodicts every observation:

| Prefix (len) | Leaked key (len) |
| -- | -- |
| `community.lexicon.calendar.rsvp/` (32) | `computer.aetheros.id/self` (25) |
| `coop.hypha.spores.social.takenFlower/` (37) | `dev.cocore.account.profile/self` (31) |
| `dev.cocore.compute.termsAcceptance/` (35) | `fm.teal.alpha.actor.status/self` (31) |
| `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization/` (40) | all 774 leaked keys are ≤ 37 chars |

The "skipped collections" mystery dissolves: `dev.cocore.compute.provider/3…` is 41 chars — longer than the 40-char prefix — so it hit the comparison, compared `Greater`, and broke its node's scan. The leak is governed by **key length vs. prefix length**, not node topology. A "healthy" collection is just one whose trailing neighbours happen to have long keys.

## Consequences for the fix

1. **The regression test is much easier than the description says.** No node-boundary engineering needed: one record in a long-named collection plus one record at a short key (e.g. `zz.a/self`) reproduces it in a `MemoryBlockStore`.
2. **No version-bump escape:** 0.1.8 (2026-03-26) is the latest release, and upstream `main`'s `entries_with_prefix` is byte-identical — still broken. Checked 2026-07-25. The local defensive fix in `list_records_json` (filter on `strip_prefix`'s `None`, break on first non-match) is required regardless; report upstream with the short-key repro.
3. `keys_prefixed` delegates to `entries_prefixed`, so any caller of either is affected — the call-site audit should cover both.

## Preserved artifacts

`linear-export/mm-473-artifacts/` (gitignored — personal repo data, never commit):

* `repo-2026-07-25.car` — the frozen sync.getRepo export the probe ran against (the live MST drifts with every write)
* `probe-output.txt` — full probe output (all 774 leaked keys, per-collection verdicts)
* `README.md` — summary + provenance

The throwaway probe test itself was deleted; it is reconstructable from this issue (open the CAR with `CarStore`, walk `tree().entries()` for ground truth, `entries_prefixed` per failing collection, diff).

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.

Settled by walking the live exported CAR (6,409 MST entries) with `atrium_repo`'s own `Tree` API. `entries_prefixed(prefix)` yields keys **outside** the requested prefix.

| Collection | Real records | `entries_prefixed` yielded | Leaked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `community.lexicon.calendar.rsvp` | 1 | 2 | `computer.aetheros.id/self` |
| `coop.hypha.spores.social.takenFlower` | 1 | 2 | `dev.cocore.account.profile/self` |
| `dev.cocore.compute.termsAcceptance` | 3 | 4 | `fm.teal.alpha.actor.status/self` |
| `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization` | 5 | **779** | **774 keys** |

The last row rules out "off by one at the boundary": the leak spans `fm.teal.alpha.feed.play/…` through `garden.goals.profile/self` — a contiguous run that **skips** the collections sorting immediately after the prefix (`dev.cocore.compute.provider`, `.receipt`, `.termsAcceptance`). An entire MST subtree is being yielded. The prefix range is not being bounded correctly when it ends at a node boundary.

This is an upstream `atrium-repo` defect (`Tree::entries_prefixed`), but it is ours to defend against.

## There is no data loss

`sync.getRepo` → 200, 3,347,975 bytes. `build_car` reads every reachable CID (commit, MST nodes, and every entry's value CID) and propagates any read failure, so a successful export proves all record blocks are present. The repo is complete.

## Why it currently 500s rather than corrupting

`crates/repo-engine/src/records.rs`, `list_records_json`:

```rust
let strip = |key: &str| key.strip_prefix(&prefix).unwrap_or(key).to_string();
// ...
let full_key = format!("{prefix}{rkey}");
let value = repo.get_raw(&full_key).await?.ok_or(RecordError::NotFound)?;
```

A leaked key lacks `prefix`, so `unwrap_or(key)` keeps it whole and the re-concatenation produces e.g.
`"dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization/garden.goals.profile/self"` — which resolves to nothing → `NotFound` → 500.

**This fallback is the only thing preventing a silent data-integrity breach.** Verified against the real repo: every leaked key resolves successfully under `get_raw` when passed *verbatim*. Had the code reused the original `key` instead of rebuilding one — the natural "optimization" — all 774 foreign records would have been returned to the caller as members of `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization`, with valid CIDs and no error.

Any fix must preserve fail-closed behaviour. Do not "fix" this by passing the original key through.

Filter on `strip_prefix`'s `None` instead of `unwrap_or`. Since the stream is ascending and foreign keys sort after the prefix range, `break` on the first non-matching key is both correct and a performance win — today a `limit=100` request against a 5-record collection walks 100 entries.

coop.hypha.spores.social.takenFlower    limit=1 -> 200   limit=2 -> 500

dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization limit=5 -> 200   limit=6 -> 500
control: app.bsky.feed.threadgate       limit=100 -> 200

Blob garbage collection no longer deletes the blobs of an account whose repo walk failed. Previously, when reconciling an account errored, that account's blobs were never pinned permanent and the sweep collected them once their upload grace expired — destroying the ownership row, the stored blob, and the file, and then propagating those deletions to the mirror bucket. The sweep now excludes any account that failed to reconcile in the same pass, so blobs whose references could not be computed are never collected; such an account retains its blobs until the underlying fault is fixed.

# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a
  change has no Linear issue, use the pull request number (for example, `271`).
- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```

The CI gate requires a fragment when a pull request changes a deployable surface:

- server or shared runtime source under `crates/*/src/`, plus PDS runtime assets;
- either mobile app's frontend, native runtime source, static assets, or Tauri config;
- the public marketing site;
- the deployed MCP surfaces — the stdio Custos MCP server (`tools/mcp/src/`) and the
  credential-forwarding sidecar (`tools/mcp-sidecar/src/`, plus its image/config), which
  ships as a Railway service and re-exports the stdio server's tool surface;
- workspace runtime dependency manifests, the production image/config, or the NixOS
  runtime module.

Documentation, tests, design files, CI configuration, scripts, developer tooling, and
other repository-internal changes do not trigger the presence requirement. Any fragment
that is present is still checked for a valid name and non-empty content.

`just set-version X.Y.Z` groups all fragments into a dated Keep a Changelog release
section in `CHANGELOG.md`, then deletes the consumed fragments. This README remains.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
Bound listRecords to the requested collection's key range

atrium-repo's `Tree::entries_prefixed` is not a reliable filter. Its
per-node bounds check reads `key.get(..prefix.len())`, which yields
`None` for any leaf whose key is *shorter* than the prefix — and the
`None` arm falls through to the unconditional push meant for subtree
pointers. Such a key is emitted verbatim, from whatever collection it
belongs to. Repos in the wild carry plenty of short keys (`zz.a/self`),
so listing a long-named collection could emit hundreds of foreign keys.

`list_records_json` stripped the prefix with `unwrap_or(key)`, so a
leaked key survived whole and the re-concatenated MST key resolved to
nothing — a hard error. That fail-closed accident was the only thing
standing between the leak and serving another collection's records
under the requested one, and it made listing permanently fail for an
affected account (any limit above the collection's real size), which in
turn blocked blob reconciliation for it.

Every yielded key is now re-checked against the prefix: it counts only
when `strip_prefix` succeeds. Keys sorting before the range are skipped
and the ascending scan stops at the first key past it, so a page also
costs no more than the collection itself rather than `limit` entries of
whatever follows. `has_more`/cursor now derive from a clean set, and the
reverse branch — which materialises the whole stream — filters the same
way. The record value is still resolved through a rebuilt
`<collection>/<rkey>` key, preserving the fail-closed property.

The two other prefixed scans (`listMissingBlobs`, `checkAccountStatus`)
pass an empty prefix, where the upstream guard degenerates to a
comparison that always matches, so they are unaffected.
EOF

MM-473 is fixed and up for review: **[PR #438](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/438)** — Linear moved to In Review with the PR attached.

## What changed

One function, [records.rs:409](crates/repo-engine/src/records.rs:409). The prefix-scan stream is no longer trusted; every key is re-classified locally:

```rust
let classify = |key: &str| match key.strip_prefix(prefix.as_str()) {
    Some(rkey) => Scan::Take(rkey.to_string()),
    None if key > prefix.as_str() => Scan::Stop,
    None => Scan::Skip,
};
```

Both traversal branches (ascending and the materialising `reverse` one) go through it, so `has_more`/cursor now derive from a clean set. The record value is still resolved via a rebuilt `<collection>/<rkey>` key — the fail-closed property you flagged is untouched.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The issue prescribed a bare `break` on first non-match. That's *almost* right: given the real root cause (short keys bypass the bounds check entirely, not a node-boundary miscalculation), a leaked key can sort **before** the prefix as well as after — `aa.bb.cc/self` leaks into a scan for `dev.cocore.…`. A bare `break` on the first non-match would have truncated that collection to zero records. `Skip`-below / `Stop`-above keeps the perf win and stays correct in both directions.
- `Stop` is sound because of a lexicographic identity worth stating: if `k > prefix` and `k` doesn't *start with* prefix, then `k` differs from prefix at some index inside the prefix with a greater byte — so `k` exceeds *every* string carrying that prefix. Ascending order then guarantees nothing further can match.
- The audit came back clean: `listMissingBlobs` and `checkAccountStatus` both pass `""`, where the upstream guard degenerates to `key.get(..0) == Some("")` and always compares `Equal`. The bug needs a *non-empty* prefix to bite.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Tests

Two regression tests build a repo with `dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization` (3 records) flanked by short keys on both sides, then sweep `limit` 1..=8 × both directions, asserting the page holds exactly that collection's records, each value is the one stored under the collection's own key, and the cursor reflects the real size. I verified they **fail** against the pre-fix `unwrap_or` semantics (temporarily reinstated, then reverted) and pass with the fix.

Verified first-hand against the worktree manifest — the main checkout is on `main`, and my first run silently tested it (84 tests instead of 86) before I re-ran with `--manifest-path`:
- `cargo test -p repo-engine` — 86 + 18 green
- `cargo test -p pds` — green
- `cargo clippy -p repo-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt -p repo-engine --check` — clean
- `changelog.d/mm-473.fixed.md` added; no ticket refs in `.rs`

## Left undone

Reporting upstream to `atrium-repo` with the short-key reproduction. It's called out as an open follow-up in the PR body — say the word and I'll draft the issue.
